messages.content:
Three independent readers read the same non-disclosure agreement (NDA) and decided whether it supports one statement (the hypothesis). They may agree or disagree, and a program has checked each of their quotes against the document. Your job is to make the final decision yourself, from the document.

<document>
<document 23 omitted, sha256 2f8e9fb245dcc4c5>
</document>

<hypothesis>
Agreement shall not grant Receiving Party any right to Confidential Information.
</hypothesis>

<readings>
<reading id="A">
label: Entailment
confidence: 72
reason: Clause 5.3 keeps all Confidential Information with the Discloser and states that disclosure gives the Recipient no licence or other rights beyond those contained in the Agreement, which supports the hypothesis that the Agreement grants the Receiving Party no right to Confidential Information.
<quote check="exact">All Confidential Information shall remain the property of Discloser or its relevant Representative, as applicable.</quote>
<quote check="exact">beyond the rights contained in this Agreement</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="B">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 70
reason: As written, clause 5.3.2 says disclosure shall give the Recipient a licence or other rights beyond those in the Agreement, which is the opposite of granting no rights.
<quote check="exact">shall give Recipient or its Representatives a licence or other rights in relation to that Confidential Information beyond the rights contained in this Agreement</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="C">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 60
reason: Clause 5.3.2 as written says disclosure gives the Recipient a licence or other rights in the Confidential Information, which conflicts with the hypothesis, although the heading 'no rights intended' points the other way.
<quote check="exact">The disclosure of Confidential Information to Recipient or its Representatives shall give Recipient or its Representatives a licence or other rights in relation to that Confidential Information beyond the rights contained in this Agreement.</quote>
</reading>
</readings>

The readings are evidence about where to look, not votes: a majority can be wrong, and a quote marked "missing" was not found in the document. Read the relevant parts of the document yourself.

Choose exactly one label:
- Entailment: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is true.
- Contradiction: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is false.
- NotMentioned: the document does not address the hypothesis, or says too little to decide.

Evidence is required. For Entailment or Contradiction, give 1 to 3 quotes copied character for character from the document (no paraphrase, no ellipses), each as short as it can be while still carrying the point. They will be checked against the document. For NotMentioned, give an empty list.

Give a confidence from 0 to 100: your probability, in percent, that your label is correct. Give a one-sentence reason.

Answer only with the JSON object the response format asks for: label, confidence, quotes, reason.

content.text: {"label": "Contradiction", "confidence": 62, "quotes": ["shall give Recipient or its Representatives a licence or other rights in relation to that Confidential Information"], "reason": "As written, clause 5.3.2 states that disclosure shall give the Recipient a licence or other rights in the Confidential Information, which contradicts the hypothesis despite the 'no rights intended' heading."}
